q: A spectrometer is a scientific instrument used to separate and measure ____ components of a physical phenomenon.
e: A spectrometer separates and measures spectral components, usually with a collimator, a disperser and a telescope. Wavelengths then fingerprint the source. A microscope magnifies shape; it does not by itself sort colour this way.

q: The optical spectrometer consists of light source, collimator, dispersion elements and a ____.
e: A refracting astronomical telescope wants a long-focus objective and a short-focus eyepiece. The final image for a relaxed eye is virtual, inverted and magnified. A wide objective gathers light and improves resolution. fs is the frequency the source emits; vs is how fast the source moves through the still medium.

q: The collimated beam from a specific light source is dispersed by dispersion element such as prism or ____.
e: A diffraction grating is many equal slits with equal opaque gaps. N is lines per unit length and d = 1/N; maxima still follow d sin theta = m lambda. Red bends more than violet in a given order; a CD is a reflection grating.

q: The angle of dispersion information is used to determine the wavelength and hence the chemical make up of the ____.
e: fs is the frequency the source emits; vs is how fast the source moves through the still medium. Source toward the observer raises pitch; source away lowers it. v without a subscript is the wave speed in the medium. Monochromatic work uses one lambda so patterns do not smear.

q: In a spectrophotometer, dispersion element separates light into ____ which is allowed to fall on the sample to be investigated.
e: spectrophotometer and dispersion have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of spectrophotometer would describe a different law.

q: The change in the absorption and ____ of the light intensity with wavelength allows for the identification of the materials.
e: Wavelength sets fringe spacing, diffraction angles and colour order on a grating. Longer lambda, larger angle in d sin theta = m lambda, so red sits farther out than violet. Monochromatic work uses one lambda so patterns do not smear. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself.
